EDGE-pos1.label: violation
EDGE-pos1.note: The delivery use case loads the console notifier adapter with a dynamic import() to log a cancelled part.

EDGE-pos2.label: violation
EDGE-pos2.note: The order use case takes the parts supplier's response type with an inline type modifier import to log the raw order.

EDGE-pos3.label: violation
EDGE-pos3.note: The application's public index publishes the parts gateway adapter with export *, and the composition root takes it from there.

EDGE-pos4.label: violation
EDGE-pos4.note: The parts gateway moves to src/domain/suppliers/ as an adapter class; the spec puts that folder in the domain layer, and the file imports the SDK.

EDGE-twin1.label: clean
EDGE-twin1.note: A domain index barrel re-exports the domain types, and the persistence adapter imports through it; adapters may depend on domain.

EDGE-twin2.label: clean
EDGE-twin2.note: The composition root loads the console notifier adapter with a dynamic import(); config may depend on adapters.

EDGE-twin3.label: clean
EDGE-twin3.note: The parts gateway imports the supplier's types with an inline type modifier; an outbound adapter may depend on the vendor.

EDGE-twin4.label: clean
EDGE-twin4.note: A new staff kiosk entry point sits in src/entrypoints/; the spec adds src/entrypoints/** to the inbound adapter layer, so it may call the inbound port.

KEY-pos1.label: violation
KEY-pos1.note: The webhook passes the raw fulfilment word; the use case maps it with an === chain over the parts supplier's fulfilment words.

KEY-pos2.label: violation
KEY-pos2.note: The supplier port carries the raw wood grade; the domain looks it up in an index-signature object literal keyed by the supplier's grade words.

KEY-twin1.label: clean
KEY-twin1.note: The domain adds a bench-days table keyed by the workshop's own instrument kinds.

KEY-twin2.label: clean
KEY-twin2.note: Same fulfilment === chain as KEY-pos1, but it sits in the webhook adapter, which hands the core its own delivery stage.

SET-pos1.label: violation
SET-pos1.note: The webhook hands the raw fulfilment word to the core; the domain copies the parts supplier's six fulfilment states as a const array and the use case casts the port's text to it.

SET-pos2.label: violation
SET-pos2.note: The supplier port carries the parts supplier's raw wood grade; the domain copies its four grades as a union and the repair job casts the port's text to it.

SET-twin1.label: clean
SET-twin1.note: The core adds its own timber quality set (premium, standard, economy), mapped from the parts supplier's four wood grades in the gateway.

SET-twin2.label: clean
SET-twin2.note: The workshop assigns each job to its own bench (WORKSHOP, SPRAY_BOOTH, SETUP_BENCH) through the HTTP adapter; it shares one of the supplier's four grade words by coincidence.

WORD-pos1.label: violation
WORD-pos1.note: The repair job gains a field named crate, the parts supplier's field name for its shipping crate id, set from the delivery port.

WORD-pos2.label: violation
WORD-pos2.note: The core part availability replaces its own delayed with backorder, the parts supplier's field name, used as a value word.

WORD-twin1.label: clean
WORD-twin1.note: The repair job gains grade, the workshop's own 1 to 5 condition grade at intake, declared in the spec glossary; the parts supplier also has a field grade.

WORD-twin2.label: clean
WORD-twin2.note: The repair job gains colour, the varnish colour the owner asked for; colour is a generic word that the parts supplier also uses.
